claims.explanation: SDM25N is an opioid receptor antagonist that also inhibits dengue virus replication by targeting the viral NS4B protein, but in cancer cells its selective killing pattern is best explained by TP53 loss combined with activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway (via PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutation, or KRAS/BRAF mutation), which creates a dependency on stress-response and survival signaling that SDM25N disrupts. The most sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 mutations together with PTEN/PIK3CA/KRAS/BRAF alterations, whereas resistant lines often retain wild-type PTEN or lack these co-occurring lesions. This suggests that SDM25N selectively kills cancer cells with defective p53 and hyperactive PI3K/AKT signaling, possibly through off-target effects on cellular stress and survival pathways.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines and rare in resistant lines
PTEN loss co-occurs with TP53 mutation in many sensitive lines and activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling
PIK3CA mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may create dependency on PI3K/AKT signaling
KRAS mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines and activate downstream survival pathways
BRAF mutations are found in sensitive melanoma and other lines, potentially sensitizing to pathway inhibition
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling and appears in several sensitive lines
RB1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may impair cell cycle checkpoints
CDKN2A loss is present in some sensitive lines and may enhance sensitivity to stress
KMT2D mutations are recurrent in sensitive lines, possibly altering chromatin and drug response
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may affect DNA repair and survival
EGFR-mutant lung lines are present in both sensitive and resistant groups, but some resistant lines carry EGFR mutations, suggesting a possible protective role
SF3B1 mutations appear in resistant lines and may alter splicing to reduce drug sensitivity
